speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what measures are ongoing to enhance public awareness of special needs children and the needs of the parents and caregivers of special needs children; and (b) how can the Ministry encourage employers and the broader community to facilitate better workplace support, such as flexible working arrangements, for parents of children with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The campaign aims to create greater awareness and improve understanding of persons with disabilities, including children with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These efforts would need to extend to our built environment as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When employers and co-workers are supportive and understanding of parents' caregiving needs, this not only makes it easier for these parents to care for their children, including those with special needs, but also benefits employers by helping them attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Family-friendly practices can bring great benefit, including raising staff morale, productivity and loyalty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Employers can tap on various resources available to implement flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is said that it takes a whole village to raise a child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the same vein, we need the support and partnership of the people, private and public sectors to build a more inclusive society.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I just wanted to raise one supplementary question.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In my home visits in Clementi, I have met mothers with special needs children who sometimes felt unsupported by employers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was wondering whether MSF has plans to engage more directly with employers, including with the human resource (HR) teams, and employees in some workplaces to further increase awareness and understanding of special needs children and the challenges that parents of special needs children face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yes, indeed, as Members can see from the answer, we have been reaching out to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have said, it takes the support and partnership of the public, private and people sectors to make our society more inclusive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I want to thank the Member for that suggestion.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for his constant support for this community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, putting up more information using Smart Nation strategies at the public places of interest and also at places, such as Mass Rapid Transit train stations, for example?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I see that in quite a number of countries which are more progressive in this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second is also if MSF would consider using good establishments or proven organisations, such as the Pioneer Generation Office (PGO), to include younger people with disabilities in their efforts so that, as they reach out to the elderly, some of whom are disabled, they are also able to reach out to the younger ones who may be disabled or need some support by their family members.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, just two efforts: one, more public awareness at more public places; second, using proven establishments to support these public awareness efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If Members have the time, please take a look at the YouTube videos.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is not only something that we want to relate to people, but I am very heartened to see the number of views that we have recorded since we launched the different videos, and the support that we get from the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to do this and we will also look at areas where we can put posters and messages, as suggested by the Member, to see how we can reach out to more people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is important for us to work together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, in my area, there has been more than one occasion where my PGO officers shared with me and we have gone down to see how we can help the families better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will do all we can to make Singapore more inclusive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, I am very heartened that we have Members in this House who care and continue to work with us to make Singapore a more inclusive society.
